Implement class SSEParser with feed(chunk: bytes) -> list[dict] and finish() -> list[dict]. It incrementally parses an SSE byte stream. Each returned event has exactly {"event": str, "data": str, "id": str, "retry": int|None}. Decode UTF-8 incrementally with replacement for malformed input. Ignore exactly one initial U+FEFF BOM; subsequent BOMs are ordinary text. Lines terminate at LF, CR, or CRLF, including terminators split between chunks. A CR ends a line immediately; a following LF is swallowed. A blank line dispatches only if at least one data field was seen, joining data field values with LF and defaulting event to "message" when the event field is empty. After every blank line, reset data/event buffers; id and retry persist globally. Lines starting ':' are comments. Split other lines at their first colon, or use an empty value when there is no colon; strip exactly one leading ASCII space from the value. Recognized fields: data, event, id, retry; ignore others. An id containing U+0000 is ignored, otherwise it replaces the persistent id, even on a block with no data. retry replaces persistent retry only for a nonempty sequence of ASCII digits 0..9; interpret as base 10. id starts as "", retry as None. Empty data fields count as data. finish flushes the decoder and processes an unterminated final nonempty line, but never synthesizes a blank line: an undispatched block is dropped. Events produced by the final decoder flush are returned by finish. A second finish returns []; feed after finish raises ValueError. Calls may contain empty byte chunks. Events must be emitted as soon as their terminating blank line is available, not held until finish.

Every operation has integer t, and times are nondecreasing; before EACH operation, purge entries with expires_at <= t. Keys are strings and stored values are integers. Entries are ordered least to most recently used. Operations: {op:"put",t,key,value,ttl}, {op:"get",t,key}, {op:"delete",t,key}, {op:"items",t}, {op:"resize",t,capacity}. put computes expires_at=t+ttl. Otherwise overwrite/insert, mark most recently used, evict LRU entries until size<=capacity, return None. get returns the value (including 0) and marks MRU, or returns None when absent. delete returns whether a live entry existed. items returns [[key,value],...] in LRU-to-MRU order and does not touch recency. resize replaces capacity with its nonnegative integer argument, evicts LRU entries if needed, and returns None. Implement path_glob(pattern: str, path: str) -> bool. Match the WHOLE logical path, case-sensitive by Unicode code points. Empty path represents zero segments. Nonempty paths have nonempty slash-separated segments, no leading/trailing/doubled '/', and neither '.' nor '..' segments; paths given to you always satisfy this. Pattern may be empty, which matches only empty path; other patterns must also have nonempty slash-separated segments and no leading/trailing/doubled '/', else raise ValueError. Within an ordinary pattern segment, '*' matches zero or more code points, '?' exactly one, and backslash escapes the next code point as a literal. A trailing backslash in any segment is invalid and raises ValueError. A slash is always a segment separator and cannot be escaped; consequently any segment ending in backslash is invalid. All other characters, including [], . and !, are literal. A segment that is exactly the two UNESCAPED characters '**' matches zero or more complete path segments. '**' embedded in a longer segment has the ordinary repeated-star meaning. Multiple '**' segments are allowed. Validate the ENTIRE pattern before returning even if an earlier segment already mismatches. No filesystem access or path normalization. Examples: 'a/**/b' matches 'a/b' and 'a/x/y/b'; '*' does not match empty path; '**' does; escaped '\*' matches a literal star segment.

Coupon can exceed subtotal. Example: three one-cent lines with one-cent coupon allocate that cent to the first line.

Implement resolve_records(events:list[dict]) -> {"values":dict,"tombstones":list[str],"accepted":list[str],"rejected":list[str]}. This is an explicitly defined batch conflict resolver for ATOMIC multi-record updates, not ordinary per-key LWW. Each event has unique-intent string id, nonnegative integer ts, string actor, and nonempty writes:dict[str,JSON_value]. A write value None is a tombstone. Duplicate event ids with EXACTLY identical entire event payload are collapsed; dict key order is irrelevant, list order matters, and JSON booleans are distinct from numbers; int/float numeric equality is allowed. The same id with any differing payload invalidates the whole batch and raises ValueError. Resolve deduplicated events in descending tuple order (ts,actor,id). Initially no keys are claimed. Accept an event if NONE of its write keys has already been claimed by an accepted event; then atomically claim ALL its keys and record all its writes. If ANY key is claimed, reject the entire event; its other keys remain unclaimed and can be claimed by later lower-ranked events. There is no partial acceptance, fallback merge, or replay order dependence. Tombstones claim keys just like ordinary writes. values contains final non-null values for claimed keys; tombstones is sorted claimed keys with null values. accepted/rejected contain ids in the actual descending-rank processing order (each id once). Returned nested values must be independent copies of the input; modifying returned values must not modify caller data. Ids are global across actors. Reordering input or dict key order must not change output.
